props.title: Surprise
lines: History is the study of surprises. It is a bad map of the next surprise.
The most important events are the ones nobody predicted. Plan for that, not for a repeat.

props.title: U.S. history, as the book lists it

rows.v: 1.3 million Americans died fighting nine major wars.
Roughly 99.9% of all companies that were created went out of business.
The stock market fell more than 10% from a recent high at least 102 times.
Annual inflation exceeded 7% in 20 separate years.
The book: 0.00000000004% of people were responsible for much of the last century's direction.
About $1.6 trillion in student loans with a 10.8% default rate — a surprise the prior generation did not budget.
The four most dangerous words: this time is different. Templeton still admitted it is different at least 20% of the time.

props.kicker: HISTORY IS A LIST OF SURPRISES
props.title: Do not treat the last war as the next one

rows.v: More than 10% off a recent high, at least 102 times. Surprise is the base rate.
Roughly 99.9% of companies ever created went out of business. Failure is normal.
Inflation over 7% in 20 separate years. Your parents' price world is not a law.
$1.6 trillion of student loans, 10.8% default — a mass product the 1950s planner did not have.
Templeton's warning still allows that it is different at least 20% of the time. Plan for both.

props.title: Forecast less, buffer more
items: The next big event will not be in last decade's textbook. Room for error is how you admit that.
Do not require a precise story of 2035. Require a life that survives a story you did not write.
